title: Grateful Dead Live at Stanley Theatre on 1972-09-28
source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Cassette -> Dat -> CD

ai_review.summary: A monster 9/28/72 show with smoking He's Gone and The Other One, captured on a crisp Miller soundboard (with a few vocal gaps).
ai_review.review: The September 28‑1972 Stanley Theatre run is hailed as one of the band’s finest – He’s Gone erupts into a funk‑laden bass frenzy, The Other One stretches to epic heights and the transitions through Me & Bobby McGee, Wharf Rat and Sugar Magnolia are seamless.  The Miller SBD source is generally clear and balanced, though Loser’s vocals are missing and a few patches/pitch‑corrections were required.

ai_rating.rationale: Overwhelmingly positive reviews (all 5‑star) praise the musical performance and note only minor recording quirks; the show is consistently described as a top‑tier Dead concert.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clear mix with excellent instrument separation.  Loser lacks vocal track, Truckin' comes from audience source, and the composite required slight pitch‑correction and patching.

standout_songs: China Cat > I Know You Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set builds strong momentum with a powerful China‑Rider and high‑energy Playing; second set launches into an explosive He's Gone that lifts the whole concert, leading to extended jams on The Other One and a soaring close.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for scorching solos (tiger stuff), inventive weaving behind Weir, and overall guitar brilliance throughout the show.
band_member_comments.Phil: Described as delivering “sheets of sound” on He's Gone – funky high‑speed runs and a memorable bass solo that many call his best ever.
band_member_comments.Bob: Highlighted for prominent rhythm work, UniVibe‑colored tone, and creative comping especially during Me & Bobby McGee and Wharf Rat.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith is noted as low in the mix or occasionally absent but still delivers some great moments later in the set.
